name: Basilides

findings.what: The 'later' test is not shown for Alexandria (census start 150) or Montanism (165). The row's only date is 'active c. 130' and gives no death year, and both traditions start within 50 years of it. The Library's own Clement says the heresy founders of Hadrian's time 'extended to the age of Antoninus the elder, as, for instance, Basilides'. Antoninus reigned to 161, so Basilides may have lived past 150. If Alexandria drops, the pass rests on Rome (200) plus Montanism (165, after 161), and those two are the same six Refutation passages shelved twice. So the doubt's sentence 'the count passes on Alexandria (7) plus Rome (6)' is not sound as stated. The recommendation stays hold on the own-words ground.
findings.fix: State in doubts that his last year is unsourced. Clement puts him into Antoninus Pius's reign (to 161), so Alexandria's 150 start may not be later. Without Alexandria the pass rests on Rome plus Montanism, which is one witness (Hippolytus) shelved twice. Recommendation stays hold.

why: Counts match, but Alexandria's start (150) may not follow his death (Clement puts him into Antoninus Pius's reign), so the stated basis for passing needs a caveat; hold stands.
